name: New Jersey
gaps: The trade-in deduction is applied as in New Jersey's sales tax practice; no Division of Taxation page stating it was opened during this reading.
Cars of exactly 3,500 lb are placed in the under-3,500 lb class; the MVC table says 'under' and 'over' 3,500 lb without naming the boundary.
The ZEV fee after July 2028 is assumed to stay at $290: the law as summarized by the MVC adds $10 a year for four years after 2024 and says nothing after.
No dealer documentation fee cap was found in the MVC and Taxation pages read.

summary.docFeeNote: No cap found in the official pages read for this release.
summary.inspectionWhere: Safety and emissions inspection every two years, after a five-year exemption for new cars; 100% electric vehicles are exempt. Free at state inspection facilities, for a fee at licensed private facilities.

singular: A new car bought in New Jersey must be registered for four years at once, so the first registration bill is about four times the yearly one [calc-js].
The yearly fee depends on two things only: whether the car weighs under or over 3,500 lb ($32 or $57 of base fee) and whether it is within two model years ($12.50 more) [regfees].
Each registration also carries a $7.50 fee and a $7 fee that the MVC's own calculator adds per year, which is why the published totals are $46.50 to $84 [calc-js].
Zero-emission cars pay an extra yearly fee created in 2024: $250 at first, then $10 more each July, $270 for registrations from July 2026 [regfees].
A new ZEV pays four years of that fee with its four-year registration: for one registered between July 2026 and June 2027, the years 2026 to 2029 [regfees].
Electric cars lost their sales tax exemption: since July 1, 2025 they pay the full 6.625% [zev-tax].
Inspections come every two years, but a new car gets a five-year exemption, and all-electric cars are never inspected [insp].
A title costs $60, or $85 with a lien [regfees].

insp.quote: Vehicles need to be inspected once every two years in New Jersey with the exception of new vehicles. New vehicles need a five-year inspection. [FAQ: exempt ... 100% Electric vehicles; private facility ... for a fee]
